title: Measles immunity: what's needed vs what we have (percent)

source.name: Vaccination Coverage and Exemptions among Kindergartners (SchoolVaxView), 2024-25 school year
source.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; herd-immunity threshold per CDC and WHO

notes: CDC and WHO put the measles herd-immunity threshold at 95 percent, the highest of any routinely vaccinated disease - it follows from the herd-immunity formula (R0 minus 1) divided by R0 at the top of measles' R0 range of 12-18. US kindergarten MMR coverage was 92.5 percent in 2024-25, down from 95.2 percent in 2019-20; about 286,000 kindergartners started school without a documented complete MMR series, and the overall exemption rate hit a record 3.6 percent.
